title: Send Capsule
trigger: A user submits sendable content and the existing submit path enters isSendBusy.
behavior: The circular send control briefly seals around the arrow, then passes a tiny capsule upward into the transcript edge while the composer stays ready for continued work.
settled: The button becomes the existing busy spinner and the capsule is gone within 220 ms; accepted content appears through the normal message flow.
failure: A rejected submit never launches the capsule. A synchronous error restores the ordinary send control and preserves the existing error text and draft.
verification: Test accepted, rejected, double-submit, keyboard, and background cases. Reduced motion swaps directly to busy state. No idle animation, timer after settlement, layout shift, focus move, or extra network event.
appleLesson: Messages effects: expressive intensity should follow a deliberate act and remain attached to its context.

title: Stash Card Tuck
trigger: The existing stash action successfully adds one prompt entry and increments pulseKey.
behavior: A paper-thin card carrying two prompt lines folds once and tucks behind the bookmark shoulder tab; the count lands on its corner like an index number.
settled: Only the existing static bookmark and count remain after 240 ms, with the saved entry available in the current keyboard-first stash menu.
failure: If persistence or image encoding fails, the card returns to the composer and existing dropped or unreadable image copy remains authoritative; deletion gets no shred effect.
verification: Test one save per pulseKey, rapid saves, image-pending entries, restore, deletion, remount, and focus retention. Reduced motion updates the count immediately. No idle animation or persistent decorative DOM.
appleLesson: Genie minimization: a short spatial handoff can explain where an object went.

title: Mode Tool Collar
trigger: The user changes the existing interaction or runtime mode control.
behavior: A small collar around the mode icon turns one indexed notch and reveals the selected tool silhouette, making Ask, Plan, and Build feel like choosing a fitted instrument.
settled: The selected silhouette and explicit mode label remain static; the composer geometry and submit behavior are unchanged.
failure: Unsupported or stale modes fall back to the current neutral control and text. Provider changes that invalidate a selection settle immediately to the supported mode without choreography.
verification: Test pointer and keyboard selection, provider invalidation, narrow layout, labels, contrast, and RTL. Reduced motion swaps silhouettes without rotation. No idle animation, hover loop, or mode inference from decoration.
appleLesson: Pencil Pro tool shadows: a visual illusion can make the active tool easier to recognize.

title: Archive Shelf Transit
trigger: The archive command succeeds for a visible thread through the shared thread action path.
behavior: The affected row compresses into a slim labeled spine and travels toward the Archive destination before list reflow closes the gap.
settled: The row is absent from the active list and present in Archived exactly as current state dictates; neighboring rows occupy their final positions.
failure: A failed or interrupted archive leaves the row in place with current error handling. Restore reverses state with a short shelf-to-row reveal only when initiated locally.
verification: Test confirmed success, failure, active-thread navigation, undo or restore, virtualization, reconnect, and rapid actions. Reduced motion performs immediate list reflow. No idle animation or replay on hydration/remount.
appleLesson: Genie minimization: movement should identify the destination of a location change.

title: Snooze Envelope
trigger: The snoozeThread mutation returns success for the requested thread and snoozedUntil value.
behavior: The thread row folds into a quiet envelope; its timestamp becomes a small address line before the envelope slips into the snoozed group.
settled: The snoozed section shows a static envelope-edge glyph beside the explicit wake time; waking restores the normal row and status text.
failure: Invalid dates, rejected mutations, or clock changes keep the row and exact error copy. Automatic wake uses a static reveal and never pretends the user acted.
verification: Test preset/custom times, timezone changes, automatic wake, manual wake, failure, replay, and list density. Reduced motion changes groups immediately. No idle animation, ticking ornament, or client-only wake truth.
appleLesson: Dashboard reverse side: one object can keep a recognizable identity across two states.

title: Pinned Tack Handoff
trigger: A local pin or unpin command is confirmed by the thread's persisted pinned state.
behavior: A tiny tack drops through the row corner and the row glides into the pinned rail; unpin lifts the tack before the row returns to normal sorting.
settled: The row rests in its state-derived section with the existing pin affordance and accessible label, and the tack becomes a static icon.
failure: Failed commands return the row to its previous section and preserve the current notification. Remote pin changes reflow without playing a local-action performance.
verification: Test pin, unpin, sorting, remote updates, duplicate events, keyboard menus, touch targets, and large lists. Reduced motion reorders instantly. No idle animation, bouncing tack, or lost focus.
appleLesson: Working icons: a tiny mark can explain an actual state rather than merely decorate it.

title: Searchlight Aperture
trigger: A debounced workspace query resolves with a new result set.
behavior: A restrained aperture at the query edge opens once, and matching path segments appear as illuminated cutouts while surrounding result chrome stays still.
settled: The aperture becomes a static search glyph and normal highlighted result text remains fully readable and selectable.
failure: Empty, failed, stale, and superseded queries use existing status copy. Late results never reopen the aperture or displace the current selection.
verification: Test stale responses, empty and error states, keyboard traversal, long paths, RTL, and large result sets. Reduced motion updates highlights immediately. No idle animation, sweeping beam, or per-result timers.
appleLesson: Flashlight switch detail: let an icon make a small amount of real explanatory work.

title: Palette Breadcrumb Bead
trigger: The command palette changes between its existing result pages or scoped groups.
behavior: A single bead slides along the breadcrumb rule into the newly selected scope, giving nested command and project navigation a compact sense of place.
settled: The bead rests beside the current text breadcrumb; result rows remain static and keyboard highlight remains the primary selection cue.
failure: Closing, escaping, or losing the target scope removes the bead immediately. Empty result pages retain their exact status and recovery actions.
verification: Test keyboard-only page changes, back navigation, search filtering, close, remount, and screen-reader labels. Reduced motion moves the bead instantly. No idle animation, looping travel, or focus delay.
appleLesson: Genie minimization: spatial motion can clarify a destination when navigation changes location.

title: Folder Hinge Peek
trigger: The user expands or collapses a directory in the project file picker.
behavior: The folder tab hinges open just enough for the first child line to slide from beneath it; collapse draws the line back before the tab closes.
settled: The existing tree, expansion state, chevron, labels, and selection remain; folder geometry is static in its open or closed pose.
failure: Loading, permission, and empty-directory states show their current copy and controls. Failed expansion closes the folder without suggesting contents loaded.
verification: Test deep trees, rapid toggles, lazy loading, errors, keyboard arrows, touch, virtualization, and RTL indentation. Reduced motion swaps folder poses. No idle animation or offscreen child animation.
appleLesson: Dashboard reverse side: preserve object identity while revealing a second surface.

title: Diff Accordion Fold
trigger: The user collapses or expands one file diff or invokes the existing collapse-all control.
behavior: Each file sheet folds along its header into a compact edge; collapse-all staggers only the visible sheets by distance from the pressed control.
settled: Collapsed files remain as ordinary static headers with filename and stats; expanded files return to the current code view and scroll model.
failure: Interrupted or superseded toggles snap to the authoritative collapsed set. Truncated, raw, loading, and errored patches keep their existing presentations without folding.
verification: Test single/all toggles, long diffs, sticky headers, virtualization, scroll anchors, raw/truncated patches, and keyboard controls. Reduced motion applies final heights immediately. No idle animation or code-line movement after settlement.
appleLesson: Dashboard material: an interface object can retain identity as its visible surface changes.

title: Review Margin Pin
trigger: A non-empty inline review comment is accepted by the existing onComment action.
behavior: The draft strip narrows into a paper tab and a small pin seats it on the selected line range, leaving the comment text attached to that margin.
settled: The current comment block, range association, delete control, and text remain static; the pin is decorative beside explicit comment semantics.
failure: Pending, failed, cancelled, or empty comments stay in the editable draft state. Deletion removes the tab plainly and never performs shredding around consequential review content.
verification: Test submit shortcut, pending state, retry, cancel, delete, multiple comments, keyboard focus, zoom, and line virtualization. Reduced motion swaps draft to comment. No idle animation or extra announcements.
appleLesson: Working icon detail: a small object can clarify that a comment is anchored to real lines.

title: Split View Hinge
trigger: The user selects the existing stacked or split diff view toggle.
behavior: The view icon behaves like a hinged drafting board: one plane opens into two synchronized leaves, or the leaves close into one stacked sheet.
settled: The selected toggle and current diff renderer remain fully static after 180 ms, with code position preserved where the renderer supports it.
failure: Unsupported patches or renderer remounts skip the hinge and retain the chosen labeled toggle. A superseding view choice jumps to the newest final layout.
verification: Test stacked/split toggles, large files, scroll preservation, comments, raw patches, repeated input, and keyboard activation. Reduced motion swaps icons and layout immediately. No idle animation or full-panel transform.
appleLesson: Dashboard reverse side: a bounded transform can make two presentations feel like one persistent object.

title: Terminal Tile Split
trigger: The horizontal or vertical split action successfully adds a terminal to the active group.
behavior: A narrow brass-like wedge enters the active pane edge and separates it into two fitted tiles, placing the new terminal where the split will actually appear.
settled: The wedge disappears and both terminal panes use the current splitter, focus ownership, labels, and persisted group geometry.
failure: Split-limit, creation, WASM, or session failures leave one pane and the exact existing error. Closing the new pane restores layout without reverse spectacle.
verification: Test both directions, split limit, creation failure, focus, resizing, persisted groups, remount, and shortcut labels. Reduced motion inserts the pane directly. No idle animation or terminal canvas transform.
appleLesson: Aqua material: restrained static form can give controls character while preserving readability.

title: Carbon Copy Clip
trigger: The user invokes the existing Add to chat action for a non-empty terminal selection.
behavior: A translucent carbon strip lifts from the selected lines, contracts into a labeled clip, and travels to the composer attachment rail.
settled: The composer shows the existing terminal context chip with terminal label and line range; terminal selection and focus follow current behavior.
failure: Empty, expired, superseded, or rejected selections create no clip. Clipboard and context-menu errors remain terminal system messages and never masquerade as attached context.
verification: Test mouse and keyboard flows, multiline ranges, superseded menus, expired contexts, focus, zoom, and composer placement. Reduced motion inserts the chip immediately. No idle animation or copied-text repaint.
appleLesson: Genie minimization: an object's path can explain its new location.

title: Process Curtain Call
trigger: The synchronized terminal session changes once to exited or closed and shouldHandleTerminalExit accepts it.
behavior: The live cursor becomes a hollow block, makes one small bow toward the final system message, and locks into a static end-cap at the prompt edge.
settled: The terminal keeps the existing Process exited or Terminal closed message, buffer, close action, and a static hollow cursor treatment.
failure: Crashes, initialization failures, and unknown states keep exact error text and use no bow. Repeated synchronized exit events never replay the gesture.
verification: Test exited, closed, crash, duplicate events, hidden drawer, remount, scroll position, and screen-reader text. Reduced motion shows the static end-cap. No idle animation, cursor loop, or buffer mutation.
appleLesson: Happy Mac: a tiny graphic can carry personality without taking over a functional screen.

title: Theme Sample Window
trigger: The user previews or commits a theme option in Appearance settings.
behavior: The chosen swatch slides into a miniature Electron window frame, recoloring its titlebar, sidebar, code strip, and composer as one coordinated material sample.
settled: The miniature preview is static and the real app uses the current theme application path; the selected theme name remains explicit.
failure: Invalid custom tokens, cancelled previews, or theme application errors restore the previous sample and current diagnostics. Contrast warnings stay factual and visible.
verification: Test preview/commit/cancel, custom themes, system changes, light/dark, high contrast, keyboard selection, and zoom. Reduced motion recolors instantly. No idle animation, ambient shimmer, or repeated whole-app transition.
appleLesson: Color-coordinated iMac: let one identity travel coherently across related surfaces.

title: Shortcut Keycap Jig
trigger: The keybinding recorder accepts a keyboard chord or detects a real conflict.
behavior: Captured modifiers and key arrive as separate keycaps that click into one rail; a conflict crosses the two affected rails with a visible cord knot.
settled: The current text shortcut, conflict warning, when-expression, reset controls, and accessible labels remain; keycaps are static tokens.
failure: Invalid, cancelled, duplicate, and unknown chords keep recorder focus and existing warning copy. Reset removes the custom rail without celebratory deletion.
verification: Test capture, cancel, conflict, platform labels, reset, when clauses, search, keyboard navigation, and screen readers. Reduced motion places keycaps instantly. No idle animation or keystroke-reactive decoration outside recording.
appleLesson: Clarus: attach playful character to a useful demonstration of configuration state.

title: Connection Target Tokens
trigger: A saved environment row resolves its existing BearerConnectionTarget, RelayConnectionTarget, or SshConnectionTarget tag; the separate primary section is outside this proposal.
behavior: The row carries a physical target token: linked bearer rings, a relay bridge, or an SSH key. Managed Relay keeps its existing T3 Connect caption.
settled: One static target shape sits beside the existing phase text and controls; its tag-derived label remains independent from connected, reconnecting, offline, and error state.
failure: An unknown target uses a neutral outlined token plus exact phase and recovery text. No target shape implies connection success or treats managed relay as a tunnel type.
verification: Test all three saved target tags across every connection phase, with relayManaged derived only for Relay, plus removal, narrow rows, high contrast, and RTL. Reduced motion swaps tokens. No idle animation, extra primary or managed-tunnel token, or inferred target.
appleLesson: Coordinated iMac accessories: related pieces can share identity while their function remains distinct.

title: Connection Phase Socket
trigger: A saved environment row observes its existing phase change from available or offline through connecting or reconnecting to connected.
behavior: A tiny socket receives a plug during connecting or reconnecting and seats only on connected. Available and offline park it nearby; error leaves the contacts visibly misaligned beside the exact status.
settled: The plug rests in one static pose keyed to available, offline, connecting, reconnecting, connected, or error, beside the existing status text and actions.
failure: Error preserves the connection reason, trace ID, retry, and removal controls. Hydration and remote observation render the current pose directly without replaying an arrival.
verification: Test all six renderer phases, error reasons, trace IDs, retry, hydration, duplicate transitions, remote observation, and multiple windows. Reduced motion swaps poses. No idle animation, perpetual connection pulse, or new IPC prerequisite.
appleLesson: Working Clock and Calendar icons: compact geometry should report real state.

title: Attachment Contact Sheet
trigger: A paste or file selection completes image validation and compression, adding accepted images to the composer draft.
behavior: Accepted images land as a slightly offset contact sheet, then square themselves into the attachment rail in original selection order.
settled: Normal thumbnails, filenames, remove controls, limits, and draft persistence remain; the sheet has no residual tilt after 200 ms.
failure: Oversized, unreadable, over-limit, or compression-failed images never join the sheet and retain current error copy. Partial batches animate accepted items only.
verification: Test paste/select, mixed batches, concurrent compression, limits, failures, draft restore, removal, keyboard, and touch. Reduced motion inserts ordered thumbnails. No idle animation, image decode loop, or send race.
appleLesson: Photo Booth: a visual treatment can make a media capability inviting while keeping experimentation safe.

title: Preview Film Gate
trigger: The user opens an image preview or navigates to the previous or next image in an existing preview set.
behavior: The image sits in a spare film gate; navigation advances one frame with a brief sprocket step whose direction matches the chosen arrow key or button.
settled: The selected image, filename, index, close button, and previous or next controls remain still and fully accessible.
failure: Missing previews, decode errors, close, and a one-image set skip transport motion. Rapid navigation resolves to the latest index without queued frame travel.
verification: Test open, close, wraparound, arrow keys, rapid navigation, decode error, one image, zoom, and touch. Reduced motion swaps frames immediately. No idle animation, autoplay, or background decoding for decoration.
appleLesson: Aqua material: static framing can make an object feel handled without reducing legibility.

title: Branch Railway Turnout
trigger: A branch checkout command succeeds and returns the authoritative next ref name.
behavior: The branch glyph becomes a tiny railway turnout: one rail pivots toward the selected ref and a labeled carriage crosses into the new branch.
settled: The current branch label, provider icon, worktree context, PR pill, and menu remain static after the successful checkout.
failure: Failed, interrupted, detached, or superseded checkouts return the turnout to the prior branch and preserve the existing error toast. Remote observation updates without carriage motion.
verification: Test local/remote refs, worktrees, detached HEAD, failure rollback, rapid selection, pagination, keyboard, and copy actions. Reduced motion changes labels instantly. No idle animation or optimistic success after rejection.
appleLesson: Genie minimization: a short path can make a change of destination understandable.

title: Commit Press
trigger: The commit command succeeds for the exact selected file set in the existing Git action dialog.
behavior: Selected file slips align beneath the commit button, receive one compact repository seal, and compress into a single labeled commit tile.
settled: The tile disappears into refreshed history within 260 ms; existing success text, branch state, remaining changes, and actions stay authoritative.
failure: Validation, hook, identity, detached-head, or command failures leave file slips unsealed and preserve selections, dialog state, and exact error details.
verification: Test partial/all selection, empty message, hooks, failure, remaining files, detached HEAD, keyboard, and duplicate submit. Reduced motion refreshes state directly. No idle animation or seal before command success.
appleLesson: Activity awards: object-like acknowledgment belongs only to a clearly defined accomplishment.

title: Push and Pull Counterweights
trigger: A push or pull command returns a successful pushed, pulled, or already synchronized result.
behavior: The two sync arrows become paired counterweights: the acted-on side travels once, and both weights level only when the returned branch state is synchronized.
settled: A static balanced or directional icon accompanies the existing success text and ahead or behind counts; the quick action remains immediately usable.
failure: Auth, conflict, upstream, detached-head, interrupted, and command errors leave the weights visibly unbalanced beside exact recovery copy. Already up to date never performs a victory flourish.
verification: Test push, pull, up-to-date, ahead/behind/diverged, auth and conflict failures, retries, and remote refresh. Reduced motion swaps balance states. No idle animation, pendulum loop, or state inferred before command result.
appleLesson: Working icons: miniature mechanics should explain state, while Messages effects warn against excess for routine actions.
